clauses.heading: Identity Fraud Expense > Definitions
clauses.text: “Identity fraud” means the act of knowingly transferring or using, without lawful authority, a means of identification of an “insured” with the intent to commit, or to aid or abet another to commit, any unlawful activity that constitutes a violation of federal law or a felony under any applicable state or local law.

clauses.heading: Identity Fraud Expense > Coverage
clauses.text: We will pay up to $15,000 for expenses incurred by an “insured” as the direct result of any one “identity fraud” first discovered or learned of during the policy period.

clauses.heading: Identity Fraud Expense > Covered Expenses
clauses.text: Covered expenses are: costs of notarizing affidavits and of certified mail to law enforcement, financial institutions and credit agencies; loan application fees for reapplying for a loan rejected because of incorrect credit information; telephone charges to merchants, law enforcement and financial institutions; lost wages, up to $250 per day and $5,000 in total, for time taken off work to deal with law enforcement or financial institutions; and reasonable attorney fees, incurred with our consent, to defend suits brought by merchants or collection agencies and to remove criminal or civil judgments wrongly entered against an “insured”.

clauses.heading: Identity Fraud Expense > Not Covered
clauses.text: We do not cover money, goods or services stolen or obtained through the “identity fraud”, including unauthorized charges and withdrawals; expenses arising out of a “business” of an “insured”; or expenses arising out of any fraudulent, dishonest or criminal act by an “insured” or any person acting in concert with an “insured”.

clauses.heading: Identity Fraud Expense > Deductible
clauses.text: A deductible of $250 applies to each “identity fraud” in place of the Section I deductible.

clauses.heading: Identity Fraud Expense > Duties
clauses.text: An “insured” must notify the police, and each financial institution or merchant involved, within 60 days after discovering the “identity fraud”, and send us receipts, bills and other records that support the expenses claimed.
